## User outcome

A local-first Android client discovers native Android ports, verifies the operations it can actually offer, helps with installation and game-data setup, and hands off to the selected game without making the owner its permanent tester. Rust Core remains the domain engine, Kotlin integrates Android, and React/Tauri supplies presentation.

## Current behavior and completed foundations

Reviewed 2026-10-03 at main `bebc292ac636fc52c96c1566116b2d2e80ce0e83`. [Platform](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/blob/bebc292ac636fc52c96c1566116b2d2e80ce0e83/crates/portcove-core/src/types.rs) and [launch](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/blob/bebc292ac636fc52c96c1566116b2d2e80ce0e83/crates/portcove-core/src/process.rs) currently express desktop platforms and executable/directory/process contracts; source inspection is not an Android build or device proof. Existing Android-related WebView-origin handling does not establish the host workflow.

#415 completed the original planning delivery in #416, merge `b51c2e185d7333aef6aa50120d84ab0a72d4524b`; retain its [exact evidence and local-audit limitation](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/issues/415#issuecomment-5573629890). #245 completed definition/trust design in #551; #397 completed client loading and retained contracts in #659 ([completion](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/issues/397#issuecomment-5638355085)). These foundations are consumed, not reopened. Android semantics and independent Android delivery still require their own proof.

The September 7 candidate survey and release table below are preserved dated observations, not current release identities, signer acceptance, device qualification or permission to switch a fork. #411 owns the bounded refresh for selected integration patterns; #139 owns lineage/fork authority.

## Release boundary and ownership

Live placement remains Deferred / Medium / Later / Post-1.0 / Opportunistic, Android. Implementation resumes only through normal prioritization after desktop commitments; no reverse prerequisite is added to #917/#921/#925, desktop beta/1.0, or shared definition, save, mod or recovery owners.

- #411: attributable candidate/variant facts and representative integration patterns.
- #412: explicit Android host contracts and finite end-to-end proof over shared Core.
- #413: adaptive discovery, setup, user-confirmed updates, partial management and truthful launch/state journeys.
- #414: Portcove APK signing/upgrades/distribution and evidence for the device/form-factor claims actually released.

Rust owns catalog/trust/compatibility/release decisions, source/integrity checks, plans, durable operations and recovery policy. Android owns installed-package observations; Kotlin owns package inspection, installer sessions, document grants, activity handoff, OS scheduling/notifications and lifecycle callbacks, injected into that same workflow. React/Tauri owns interaction/navigation/adaptive views. Local-first use and optional accounts remain intact.

## Observable platform-release acceptance

**Owner-approved replacement, 2026-10-03:** six distinct games across three engine families is a nonblocking lineup/coverage ambition, not an absolute prerequisite for an Android preview or release. The old gate has been superseded, not satisfied. Neither the owner personally playing every game nor completing every research candidate is a release requirement.

- [ ] Declare the preview/release's exact host API/ABI, device/form-factor, offered operations, supported integration contracts and known limitations. Keep platform readiness, variant capabilities, device compatibility and per-port evidence independent; do not collapse them into a tested/supported ladder.
- [ ] Consume #412's installed-shell proof and #413's useful complete user journeys. Use controlled lawful APKs plus a small set of real integrations that differ structurally in package/data/setup/launch behavior. Record why each pattern matters rather than imposing a game/family quota.
- [ ] Consume #414's signing, previous-APK upgrade/preservation and appropriate device evidence for claims actually made. A phone-scoped preview need not wait for handheld/controller or TV claims it does not make; those remain explicitly tracked there.
- [ ] Compatible definitions inside accepted publisher scope and implemented contracts may be available with gameplay **Not tested** after mandatory admission checks pass. Unknown package identity/signer continuity/required data access, known unsafe behavior and unsupported operations remain scoped holds/unavailable. Holds name the affected route and operation: missing update signer continuity blocks managed install/update claims; inaccessible saves block save operations. They do not automatically suppress a separately supported, non-destructive external-package launch whose exact target/intent, applicable trust policy and user authorization can be established. A route lacking its own mandatory identity/data facts remains held. An untested game is not proof of harmless execution.
- [ ] New definitions using implemented Android capabilities can reach a client built earlier under the protected delivery contract. New native mechanisms may require a client update; frozen format-1 and existing desktop/external contracts never implicitly acquire Android semantics.
- [ ] Release evidence identifies source/head, Portcove APK, exact game artifact/version/signer, platform/device, operation, method, result/date and retained diagnostics. Source inspection, fixtures, emulator execution, physical observations and gameplay/save compatibility are separate claims.

Full parent closure requires the bounded child outcomes for the declared Android scope; optional lineup expansion, future form factors and optional save/mod integrations remain separately visible and do not indefinitely hold a useful scoped preview. Known mandatory failures are not waived by the revised gate.

## Scope and non-goals

ARM64 first; Android 10 is a proposed minimum to validate in #412/#414, distinct from target-SDK policy and each game's requirements. Signed GitHub APK/manual upgrades, optional Obtainium for Portcove, shared catalog delivery and native Android games remain the plan.

No desktop-Linux emulation, desktop feature parity, root/Shizuku/broad-filesystem default, APK patching/re-signing, proprietary payload distribution, on-device game compilation, universal filesystem rewrite, daemon, parallel policy/library database or generalized plugin platform. Expected Kotlin integration is not a reason to replace Tauri. #412 owns concrete framework reconsideration evidence; no second UI stack is scheduled preemptively.

## Required future tests and documentation

Use current diff-selected policy for each implementation slice and independent review of new capability/trust boundaries. #412 owns host/failure fixtures, #413 the actual consumer journeys, #414 packaged/device/distribution evidence. Do not reproduce obsolete blanket audit commands or a full per-game lifecycle campaign for unchanged shared machinery. Appropriate agent/hosted/device/community observations are usable at their actual scope; owner-operated macOS or personal every-game tests are not required.

Stable docs describe planned architecture until implemented. Public instructions must declare Android's actual operations and qualification limits; issues/Project remain the sole executable/scheduling authorities. No working APK or new qualification is claimed by this reconciliation.

## Dependencies and resume condition

Children are organizational owners, not mutual blockers. Research and controlled fixture design may proceed independently when selected; real integration proof consumes the relevant #411 evidence, not closure of the entire pool. #412 consumes completed #397/#245; production acceptance/publication uses the applicable #246 protected path without Android blocking #246. Shared saves (#48/#252/#253), profiles/providers (#250/#262 including **GameBanana and Thunderstore**), recovery (#925) and external contracts (#30/#243) retain their own boundaries and commitments.

## Completion evidence

Planning reconciliation only. Android implementation, signing-key provisioning, published APKs and runtime/device qualification remain pending.

<summary>Historical specification and dated evidence preserved; superseded current acceptance as of 2026-10-03</summary>

The numerical release gate and blanket future validation instructions below are historical, not active acceptance. Use the execution-facing sections above. Historical observations retain their original dates and limits.

> **Planning reconciliation — 2026-09-08, #531:** Post-V1 / Opportunistic → Post-1.0 / Opportunistic. Vocabulary only; optional/deferred scope, status and priority preserved. Earlier numbered-stage timing in the retained text below is historical and superseded; scope/evidence stays required as stated. 

## User outcome
Android phone and gaming-handheld owners discover native ports, verify game files, install reviewed APKs, follow supported setup, update games, and launch them from Portcove. Reviewed Android forks and clearly disclosed partial management are accepted.

## Current behavior and evidence
Decision recorded 2026-09-07: pursue a bounded Post-V1 edition rather than skip Android. Portcove currently has four desktop platform targets and desktop process/path assumptions. The local catalog contained 67 entries, all-state issue inventory 186 Port issues, and live Project inventory 321 items during research. A five-most-recent-release survey covered 171 upstream references: three remained unavailable after retry and one malformed repository reference was corrected. This is not an exhaustive historical or device audit.

These are candidate observations, not support claims. Existing issues identify original targets; independent Android forks need separate canonical identity under #139 before admission, without reopening or replacing completed desktop owners. No APK was installed or signature/device-tested in this research.

## Scope
Tauri 2 plus shared React presentation and Rust core, with a narrow Kotlin host integration. Core owns catalog, source inspection, release/integrity decisions, operation records and supported actions. Android owns installed package truth; the adapter supplies observations and system operations. React owns presentation only. Start with Android 10+ ARM64; each game may require a higher OS/GPU level.

Use explicit Android package contracts rather than portable executable installs: artifact/upstream, package ID, versionCode, accepted signer, ABI/OS and setup capability. Use system installer confirmation and activity launch. Persist pending operations and reconcile after restart, cancellation, reboot and external updates. Do not equate downloaded with installed or activity dispatch with gameplay.

Use SAF document selection and bounded app-private source inspection; supported URI transfer or guided game-owned import. Save/mod/rollback operations are unavailable unless an exact game integration permits and qualifies them. Do not silently uninstall to repair update/signature/downgrade conflicts.

Distribute signed Portcove APKs on GitHub with stable identity/version codes and Obtainium instructions for self-updates. Game updates use Portcove's verified system-installer route; a Portcove self-updater is deferred. Keep public CLI behavior stable and version externally visible machine contracts; frozen format-1 clients must not acquire Android semantics implicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All four finite delivery children have matching evidence.
- [ ] At least six distinct games across three independent engine families pass install, setup, launch, save/reload and update preservation. Shared APKs and duplicate implementations are not independent evidence.
- [ ] Phone and gaming-handheld physical observations identify exact artifacts, sources, OS, ABI, GPU, controls and limitations; no universal device claim.
- [ ] Android host integration retains core policy authority and existing desktop safety guarantees.
- [ ] Obtainium and manual Portcove upgrades preserve settings/library metadata; release signing/recovery is qualified.
- [ ] If the six-game threshold fails, defer with exact resume conditions; do not expand into maintaining game ports.

## Required tests
Wrong digest/package/signer/ABI/source/OS; malformed/ambiguous archive; storage exhaustion; revoked document access; cancellation, offline and process-death recovery; concurrent and external package changes; upgrade data preservation; desktop regression suite; just audit and just deep for the architecture change. Physical phone/handheld and 4 KB/16 KB environments are distinct from synthetic tests.

## Dependencies and blockers
Deferred until Post-V1 capacity and the bounded qualification/integration proofs are available. Four children will own candidate qualification, integration proof, product behavior, and distribution qualification. #139 owns fork policy; #245/#397 own successor definition capabilities. Coordinate interfaces without making Android a dependency of them, #45, or any desktop release. Parentage is organizational; final distribution depends on the actual implementation and qualification children.

## Non-goals
No desktop parity requirement, emulation/translation layer, root/Shizuku, broad filesystem access, proprietary asset distribution, upstream APK repackaging/re-signing, or on-device game compilation. No desktop release gate is added. Signing authority and publication require their separately reviewed release step.

## Documentation impact
Live scheduling stays in GitHub Projects; exact evidence stays in issues. Change stable architecture, catalog, release, or user documentation only when the corresponding behavior changes. No second backlog or mutable status document.

## Completion evidence
Pending. Research and planning are not APK signature verification, installation, device execution, gameplay, save preservation, or released Android support.
